title: Gantt planning, people and history — current menus

scenes.title: Build a plan you can maintain
scenes.text: PlantUML Ultimate turns a plain text plan into a chart you can edit visually. The source remains readable and suitable for Git review. This short tour uses a few prepared examples to show task editing, people, workload and version history. Each example focuses on one planning decision. Keep the text and the chart together as you work.

actions.title: Create, organize and update the work
items: Move, resize, reorder and edit several tasks

scenes.title: Create a task with a real start
scenes.text: Add a task from the Insert tab. Give it a meaningful name and a duration in working days. Choose a start date rather than relying on an accidental default. Review the fields before adding it. The new task appears in the chart and in the source.

scenes.title: Edit a task and its effort
scenes.text: Click a task to open its inspector. Edit the duration, then leave the field to commit the change. The source records the new effort estimate. Check the chart after the edit, including tasks that depend on it. Close the inspector when you are ready to continue.

scenes.title: Record progress explicitly
scenes.text: Progress is another explicit task property. Open the task inspector. Enter twenty five percent in Progress. The matching completion statement is written into the source. Keep this observation current when reporting the project. Close the inspector to review the plan.

scenes.title: Inspect an assignment
scenes.text: People are assigned in the task inspector. Open Resources to see a person and their allocation. An allocation is a scheduling assumption. Review it alongside the effort estimate. A larger percentage needs a practical explanation, not just a desire for an earlier finish.
scenes.source:
@startgantt
title Customer portal team workload
Project starts 2026-11-02
saturday are closed
sunday are closed
[Design] as [design] on {Alice:100%} starts 2026-11-02 and lasts 5 days
[Frontend] as [frontend] on {Alice:100%} starts 2026-11-02 and lasts 8 days
[Backend] as [backend] on {Sam:100%} starts 2026-11-02 and lasts 8 days
[Testing] as [testing] on {Morgan:100%} starts at [backend]'s end and lasts 4 days
@endgantt

scenes.title: Add a second person and inspect the working duration
scenes.source:
@startgantt
title Resource allocation practice
Project starts 2026-11-02
saturday are closed
sunday are closed
[Backend] as [backend] on {Sam:50%} lasts 8 days
@endgantt
scenes.text: Here Backend has eight days of effort and one part time assignment. Open Resources to inspect that starting point. Add Alex at fifty percent as a second person. Both assignments are retained while the effort estimate stays at eight days. The working duration is calculated from the combined allocation; check the task tooltip to see the result.

scenes.title: Open the workload panel
scenes.text: Open Plan, then Workload. This example deliberately assigns Alice to overlapping tasks. The peak reaches two hundred percent against her one hundred percent capacity. Read the warning as a conflict to resolve. Click Frontend to return to the responsible task and inspect its assignment. Workload links the warning to the plan you can change.

scenes.title: Capacity is an assumption
scenes.text: Capacity changes the assumption used to evaluate workload. Open Plan and Workload. Enter a different capacity only when it represents real availability. Commit the field and compare the warning. A capacity of two hundred percent may describe a team resource; it does not create more hours for one person. Keep that distinction visible when you explain a plan.

scenes.title: Compare the exact source
scenes.text: Version history makes changes reviewable. In this example we create a checkpoint, then change the Design estimate. Open File and Version history, and select the checkpoint for comparison. Choose Source to inspect the exact changed lines. This gives a concrete record to discuss before accepting a new schedule.

scenes.title: Compare the drawing
scenes.text: The same comparison has a Rendered view. Select it to see the earlier chart beside the working copy. Review the scheduling consequence as well as the text diff. Tasks, people, workload and history all remain tied to a readable PlantUML document. Commit the text to Git and reopen it here whenever visual editing is useful.
